predecessors.name: Kingdom of Arles
predecessors.text: 'south from the Rhône to Nice and north from Embrun to the Vivarais'; a fief of the Kingdom of Arles (947-1032)

successors.name: Royal domain of France
successors.text: Charles III's will of 10 December 1481 names Louis XI 'universal heir'; 'legally incorporated into the French royal domain in 1486', 'annexed to France in 1487'

rulers.name: Ramon Berenguer (I the Great) of Barcelona

ledger.x: 947: Boson II, Count of Arles, establishes the County of Provence as a fief of the Kingdom of Arles.
1112: Douce, heiress of Provence, marries Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona and the county passes to the Catalan house.
1125: the county is partitioned and the lands north of the Durance go to the Count of Toulouse as a marquisate.
1193: the partition between the County of Provence and the County of Forcalquier ends with Alfonso II's marriage.
1246: Charles of Anjou becomes count and the Angevins rule until 1382 (Beatrice is listed as countess 1245-1267, Charles I 1246-1285).
1382: the Union of Aix rises against Louis of Anjou's succession.
28 September 1388: Nice and the Ubaye valley pass to Savoy.
10 December 1481: Count Charles III names Louis XI his heir and Provence passes to the French crown.
December 1481: the county ends with Charles III's will; Louis XI inherits it.

wars.name: Union of Aix (Provençal succession)
wars.outcome: The Union of Aix (1382-1387) opposed Louis of Anjou; the city of Nice separated in 1388.

certainty.note: Comital borders with no survey; the Durance line of the 1125 partition and the 1388 Nice dedication are treaty lines but their positions are not on the pages.

sources.title: Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona
